title: Forward-Assisted Purification: A Spatiotemporal Framework Beyond Conventional Limits
summary: Noise remains the primary obstacle to realizing quantum advantage, continuously degrading the resources that enable quantum technologies. Purification aims to reverse this degradation by extracting high-fidelity resources from noisy ensembles, yet its conventional formulation is intrinsically static, acting only after noise has taken effect. Here we instead recast purification as a dynamical task, introducing a spatiotemporal framework that distributes interventions across the noise process.
